paragraphs: An image can contain individually plausible features whose relationships are wrong, such as a shadow inconsistent with the sun or a reflection inconsistent with an object. This paper asks whether diffusion models learn the conditional rules connecting such features. It distinguishes broad visual regularities from precise inter-feature consistency.

After identifying failures in mainstream models, the authors construct four synthetic tasks with strongly correlated features. Experiments show that models capture coarse rules more readily than fine-grained ones. Their theoretical analysis finds persistent rule-learning error for denoising score matching in the studied setting, attributing it to a mismatch between the training objective and rule conformity.

Additional classifier guidance during sampling produces limited improvements. The analysis suggests that classifiers also struggle to detect the subtle signals needed for precise rules. The contribution is a diagnosis supported by controlled tasks and theory, rather than a complete solution; its findings explain why high visual quality need not imply exact relational consistency.
icml-2025-can-diffusion-models-learn-hid.tldr: Diffusion models can miss precise relationships among image features even when they learn coarse rules, and classifier guidance only partly helps.

paragraphs: Preference optimization can align image generators with text prompts, but comparing visually very different images makes the useful change ambiguous. A preferred image may differ from a rejected image in many unrelated ways. D-Fusion constructs training pairs intended to isolate alignment improvements while retaining visual consistency.

The method uses mask-guided self-attention fusion to produce well-aligned images that remain visually similar to given poorly aligned examples. It also preserves the generated images’ denoising trajectories, which are needed for the diffusion-model preference-training procedure. This makes the construction useful as training data rather than only as a final image-editing technique.

Experiments show improved prompt-image alignment when D-Fusion is used with different reinforcement-learning algorithms. The contribution is therefore a way to improve the comparability and usability of preference examples. The abstract does not quantify the gains or demonstrate that all remaining differences between paired images are irrelevant to the preference judgment.
icml-2025-d-fusion-direct-preference-opt.tldr: D-Fusion creates visually consistent preference pairs and their denoising trajectories to improve text-image alignment training.

paragraphs: Brain networks are often built from pairwise Pearson correlations between brain regions and then processed with graph models. This paper questions whether message passing is the best operation for that particular representation. Its analysis and experiments suggest that the structure of these correlation-derived networks limits the benefit of conventional message passing.

The authors observe advantages from elementwise Hadamard products over the matrix products used to express message passing. They introduce Brain Quadratic Network, or BQN, using quadratic networks with favorable approximation properties. Theoretical analysis also connects BQN’s representation learning to implicit community detection, providing an interpretation of what its computations extract.

Extensive evaluations show better performance and efficiency than the compared message-passing approaches to brain-network modeling. The contribution is tied to the stated network construction and application. It does not show that message passing is unnecessary for all graphs, nor that improved predictive results alone establish a clinically validated diagnostic system.
icml-2025-do-we-really-need-message-pass.tldr: BQN uses quadratic, elementwise computations to outperform message-passing models on the evaluated correlation-based brain networks.

paragraphs: Summarizing many people’s views into a short list of statements resembles a committee election, except the candidates are all statements that could be written. That candidate space is effectively accessed through generation and evaluation queries. This paper extends generative social choice to make the resulting summaries more realistically constrained.

The framework now provides theoretical guarantees when queries are only approximately optimal and when the total length of the selected statements is limited. Both changes matter for language-model implementations: generated candidates need not be the best possible statements, and a useful slate must fit within a concise communication budget.

Using GPT-4o to implement the queries, the authors demonstrate the method on city-improvement opinions and drug reviews. The examples support its ability to produce proportionally representative slates from unstructured input. The contribution combines a stronger theoretical model with applications; representativeness is evaluated through the framework’s social-choice criteria rather than a claim that every participant endorses every chosen statement.
icml-2025-generative-social-choice-the-n.tldr: Generative social choice gains guarantees for imperfect queries and length budgets when producing representative summaries of public opinions.

paragraphs: A repository of trained models is useful only if users can identify which model suits their task. In the learnware paradigm, each model carries a specification describing its specialties. This paper argues that matching data distributions alone overlooks how well a model actually distinguishes the outcomes relevant to a task.

Dali generates specifications through dual alignment. Alongside distribution alignment, it includes discriminative alignment to characterize the model’s predictive behavior. The specification is therefore intended to describe both the data a model relates to and the distinctions it is capable of making, giving model reuse a richer basis than distribution similarity alone.

Theoretical and empirical analyses show that the resulting specifications improve model reuse in the learnware setting. The contribution concerns model description and selection rather than training every user’s model from scratch. The abstract does not provide numerical reuse gains or detail the access needed to measure discriminative performance, which are important implementation considerations.
icml-2025-learnware-specification-via-du.tldr: Dali combines distribution and discriminative alignment to describe model specialties more effectively for reuse.

paragraphs: Diffusion-based retrieval reranks candidates by propagating similarities through a graph, helping capture the data manifold. But useful signals can fade several steps from their source, weakening discrimination outside local neighborhoods. This paper develops a transition framework intended to maintain local quality while supporting broader retrieval.

Locality Preserving Markovian Transition combines three components. Bidirectional Collaborative Diffusion connects similarity information across separate graphs. Locality State Embedding represents each instance as a distribution to preserve local consistency. A Thermodynamic Markovian Transition then links those distributions through a multi-state, long-term transition process for measuring manifold relationships.

Experiments across diverse retrieval tasks support the effectiveness of LPMT. The contribution is a coordinated re-ranking framework that addresses how similarity information travels beyond immediate neighbors. The abstract does not provide the detailed transition equations or numerical gains, so it supports the method’s structure and tested utility without establishing an identical improvement for every affinity-graph construction.
icml-2025-locality-preserving-markovian-.tldr: LPMT combines collaborative diffusion, local distribution embeddings, and Markovian transitions to improve instance-retrieval re-ranking.

paragraphs: Pipeline parallelism splits a large model across devices, but synchronized training can leave stages idle. Asynchronous updates keep the pipeline busy while introducing stale gradients computed from older weights. This paper modifies Nesterov acceleration to address that optimization cost of full pipeline utilization.

The proposed method changes Nesterov’s look-ahead step to account for gradient staleness. The authors prove sublinear convergence when the gradient delay is fixed. This provides a theoretical link between an accelerated-update mechanism and the delayed information inherent in asynchronous pipeline training.

Experiments train decoder-only language models with up to one billion parameters. The method substantially outperforms existing asynchronous approaches and even exceeds the synchronous baseline in the reported tests. The result suggests that carefully designed updates can make full pipeline use practical, while the formal guarantee’s fixed-delay assumption is narrower than every possible real-world scheduling pattern.
icml-2025-nesterov-method-for-asynchrono.tldr: A modified Nesterov look-ahead step mitigates stale gradients in asynchronous pipeline training, improving reported language-model results.

paragraphs: Some language-model tokens receive disproportionately large attention despite having limited semantic importance. This paper studies those attention sinks through hidden-state geometry, looking beyond attention weights alone. It finds that other tokens increasingly resemble a comparatively stable sink-token representation in deeper layers.

OrthoRank turns that observation into a dynamic token-selection rule. It treats tokens that remain more orthogonal to the sink token as more important, using this geometry as a proxy for how quickly their representations move toward the sink. The method therefore selects computation based on relationships among hidden states rather than simply removing whole layers.

At the same sparsity ratio and comparable throughput, experiments show lower perplexity and higher zero-shot accuracy than layer-pruning methods, alongside stronger LongBench performance. The contribution is a geometrically motivated criterion for efficient inference. The findings do not imply that every highly attended token is uninformative or that orthogonality perfectly measures semantic importance in every model.
icml-2025-orthorank-token-selection-via-.tldr: OrthoRank uses hidden-state orthogonality to attention-sink tokens to select important tokens for efficient language-model inference.

paragraphs: A visually convincing 3D object is not automatically suitable for manufacturing. Milling, casting, and injection molding require representations with practical structure and constraints that rendering-focused generators may ignore. This position paper examines that gap between attractive virtual assets and usable computer-aided manufacturing inputs.

The authors identify missing manufacturing-readable semantics, difficulty decomposing complex shapes into parameterized segments, and inadequate evaluation metrics. They also test generative CAD models beyond their training distributions and on unmodified human-created objects. Revised datasets and baseline benchmarks are provided to make the challenge more realistic and measurable.

The evaluations find substantial overfitting to simpler data and poor generalization to the proposed settings. The contribution is a diagnosis and research agenda backed by benchmark evidence. It calls attention to representational and evaluation requirements for manufacturing, rather than claiming that one new model already converts arbitrary generated 3D shapes into production-ready designs.
icml-2025-position-you-cant-manufacture-.tldr: The paper exposes a manufacturability gap in generative 3D and CAD models and supplies more realistic datasets and baselines.

paragraphs: Removing selected knowledge from a generative model can require expensive fine-tuning and access to its original training data. Large updates may also disturb useful behavior that should remain. SEMU seeks a compact way to perform machine unlearning while changing fewer parameters and avoiding that data dependency.

The method uses singular value decomposition to construct a low-dimensional projection for selective forgetting. This confines the modification to a smaller parameter representation instead of tuning substantial portions of the model. The design aims to preserve previously learned knowledge without requiring the original training dataset for stabilization.

Extensive experiments show competitive unlearning performance with improved efficiency in data usage and the number of modified parameters. The contribution is an economical unlearning mechanism. The abstract does not present a formal certificate that every trace of selected information is erased, so efficient empirical forgetting should be distinguished from a universal guarantee of complete removal.
icml-2025-semu-singular-value-decomposit.tldr: SEMU uses an SVD-based low-dimensional projection to perform competitive unlearning with fewer changed parameters and no original training data.

paragraphs: Variance reduction improves stochastic optimization by making gradient estimates less noisy, but transferring these methods to curved parameter spaces requires careful geometric handling. This paper develops a common recursive framework for nonconvex optimization on Riemannian manifolds. It aims to connect several existing estimators and derive new ones within the same analysis.

The authors first introduce a recursive gradient estimator in Euclidean space, then extend it to manifolds as SERENA. The framework includes R-SRVRG, R-SVRRM, R-Hybrid-SGD, and earlier Riemannian variance-reduction methods. A unified theory works with retractions and vector transport, the operations used to update and compare tangent-space quantities.

For two proposed methods, gradient-oracle complexity matches the stated lower bounds in finite-sum and online settings, including O(ε⁻³) in the online case. Experiments outperform compared Riemannian optimizers. The contribution combines an organizing framework with efficient algorithms, under the nonconvex and geometric assumptions of the analysis.
icml-2025-serena-a-unified-stochastic-re.tldr: SERENA unifies recursive variance reduction on manifolds and provides methods with optimal stated oracle-complexity guarantees.

paragraphs: Model stealing attempts to reproduce a black-box model from its outputs without possessing its training data. Synthetic-data approaches can help, but many assume that an attacker knows class names or can write effective prompts. This paper tests a less expertise-dependent threat model to assess the security implications of pretrained generators.

Stealix combines two open-source pretrained models to infer information about the target distribution and evolves prompts with a genetic algorithm. Iterative refinement improves the precision and diversity of synthesized images used in the replication study. The emphasis is on automating the prompting component rather than requiring a predefined prompt collection.

Under equal query budgets, experiments outperform compared methods, including some with access to class names or detailed prompts. The contribution is evidence that generative-model assistance can lower practical barriers to model replication. These benchmark results characterize the studied threat model; they do not establish that every protected model can be copied without restriction or additional assumptions.
icml-2025-stealix-model-stealing-via-pro.tldr: Stealix shows that automated prompt evolution can strengthen black-box model replication without predefined prompts or class-name knowledge.

paragraphs: Volumetric models often need to respond predictably when an object is rotated or translated. Steerable convolutions encode those transformation rules, while attention can connect information across a broader spatial extent. This paper combines the two in a Transformer architecture that preserves special-Euclidean equivariance.

The proposed attention mechanism operates on features extracted by steerable convolutions. Computation takes place in Fourier space, including the nonlinear operations. The design extends the Vision Transformer mechanism while ensuring that transformations from SE(d) lead to the corresponding structured transformation of the representation.

Experiments in two and three dimensions show that adding steerable Transformer layers improves steerable convolutional networks. The contribution is an equivariant attention extension with empirical support in both dimensional settings. The abstract does not specify the datasets, numerical gains, or computational overhead, so it establishes the architectural principle without a universal claim about efficiency or superiority over every volumetric model.
icml-2025-steerable-transformers-for-vol.tldr: Steerable Transformers add SE(d)-equivariant attention to steerable convolutional features, improving the reported 2D and 3D results.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks produce outputs across multiple time steps, and variation between those outputs can support better performance. Existing training methods create some temporal diversity through neuron dynamics and architecture. This paper argues that limited diversity in the gradients of temporal logits leaves another source of useful variation underused.

Temporal Model Calibration rescales logit gradients across time steps. The authors connect insufficient gradient diversity to temporal miscalibration, then design the rescaling mechanism to improve both. This targets the training signal directly rather than relying only on a different spiking-neuron model or network structure.

Experiments show greater temporal gradient diversity and better-performing, temporally calibrated networks. The method reaches state-of-the-art accuracy on ImageNet, DVSCIFAR10, and N-Caltech101 in the reported comparisons. The contribution concerns training quality and accuracy; although spiking networks are motivated partly by energy efficiency, the abstract does not report a measured energy reduction from this calibration procedure.
icml-2025-training-high-performance-spik.tldr: Temporal Model Calibration rescales gradients across time to improve spiking-network diversity, calibration, and benchmark accuracy.

paragraphs: A small collection of labeled anomalies rarely represents the full range of abnormal behavior. Weakly supervised anomaly detection must therefore use those scarce labels without collapsing all unusual cases into an overly narrow representation. WSAD-DT builds a latent geometry intended to separate normal and anomalous examples while preserving variation within each group.

The method uses separate normal and anomaly centroids. A light-tailed kernel compacts in-class points, while a heavy-tailed kernel maintains separation from out-of-class instances. Kernel-based regularization preserves within-class diversity. An ensemble partitions unlabeled data into varied subsets while sharing the limited labeled anomalies across those partitions.

Experiments achieve state-of-the-art performance on several challenging benchmarks and outperform leading ensemble methods such as XGBOD. The contribution combines representation geometry and data reuse under sparse supervision. The abstract does not claim detection of every unseen anomaly type, so the benchmark gains should be interpreted within the abnormal behaviors and data conditions evaluated.
icml-2025-weakly-supervised-anomaly-dete.tldr: Dual-tailed kernels and an ensemble strategy improve anomaly separation while reusing scarce labeled anomalies and preserving class diversity.

paragraphs: CLIP encoders are reused across models, tasks, and domains, so a perturbation that transfers widely could expose a shared robustness weakness. This paper investigates that possibility through X-Transfer. Its target is a single universal adversarial perturbation that remains effective across multiple kinds of changes in the evaluated system.

The method uses surrogate scaling, dynamically selecting a small suitable subset from a larger collection of candidate surrogates. This supports a broader search for transferable behavior without requiring every surrogate to participate in each computation. The paper calls simultaneous transfer across data, domains, models, and tasks super transferability.

Extensive evaluations show stronger transfer than previous universal-perturbation methods on CLIP-based models and downstream vision-language systems. The contribution is evidence of a broad vulnerability across the tested conditions and a method for studying it. Universal here describes reuse of one perturbation across examples; it does not constitute a proof that all possible CLIP deployments are vulnerable.
icml-2025-x-transfer-attacks-towards-sup.tldr: X-Transfer demonstrates a single perturbation with broad transfer across evaluated CLIP models, data domains, and downstream tasks.

paragraphs: Epidemiological simulators often require manual redesign when disease assumptions, interventions, or policies change. EpiAgent treats that redesign as an iterative program-synthesis problem. The framework aims to automate model construction while retaining interpretable mechanistic structure and explicit correctness checks.

An epidemiological flow graph serves as an intermediate representation between a scenario description and executable code. Modular checks validate the graph before it is compiled into a mechanistic model. The system then calibrates parameters under physical and epidemiological constraints and uses feedback to refine the model rather than relying on one unchecked generation.

Scenario case studies show complex growth dynamics and consistent counterfactual projections under changing vaccination and immune-escape assumptions. The feedback loop accelerates convergence toward valid models and prevents degeneration in the reported evaluation. These are model-construction and scenario-consistency results; the abstract does not establish prospective forecasting accuracy or validate the system as an autonomous public-health decision maker.
icml-2026-agentic-framework-for-epidemio.tldr: EpiAgent builds and refines mechanistic epidemic simulators through verified flow graphs and constrained parameter learning.

paragraphs: Software requests often omit information, but asking about every omission wastes effort and may demand answers users cannot provide. This paper studies which clarifications actually improve task success. It separates the usefulness of information from the practical answerability of the question used to obtain it.

The authors analyze real software-engineering tasks with Shapley attribution and distributional comparisons, while simulated users provide responses for evaluating questions. The findings motivate two reward dimensions: task relevance and user answerability. These become multi-stage reinforcement-learning rewards for CLARITI, an eight-billion-parameter clarification module.

On underspecified issues, CLARITI matches GPT-5’s resolution rate while asking 41% fewer questions. The contribution is an empirically grounded reward design for more efficient clarification, rather than a policy of always asking fewer questions. The simulated-user component is important context for the evidence; the abstract does not report the same comparison in a live study with human software users.
icml-2026-asking-what-matters-reward-dri.tldr: CLARITI learns to ask useful, answerable software questions, matching the reported GPT-5 resolution rate with 41% fewer questions.

paragraphs: Formal theorem proving checks whether a stated proposition follows, but many mathematical tasks require discovering an unknown answer first. This paper develops Formal Problem-Solving to bring that constructive step into a verifiable process. The framework uses Lean 4 so the answer and its justification are linked from the start.

An unknown answer is represented as a metavariable coupled to a proof obligation. Deductive FPS structures work into forward derivation and backward verification. The authors also create three benchmarks totaling more than 1,000 problems and introduce Restricted Propositional Equivalence, a symbolic correctness measure designed to avoid brittle dependence on exact answer strings.

Experiments with state-of-the-art provers show that solving these tasks is substantially harder than proving supplied propositions. The contribution is a formal formulation, evaluation resources, and evidence of that gap. Verification strengthens reliability for the encoded problem, while the benchmark still tests whether a system can construct the needed answer rather than merely confirm a known one.
icml-2026-beyond-theorem-proving-formula.tldr: Formal Problem-Solving couples unknown answers with Lean proof obligations and reveals a substantial gap between solving and proving.

paragraphs: Temporal-difference learning is harder to analyze for average reward than for discounted reward because the relevant Bellman operator lacks the usual contraction property. This paper introduces a policy-evaluation algorithm intended to close part of that theoretical gap. The method draws samples from two Markovian trajectories.

The authors define a projected Bellman equation with a unique solution and prove convergence to it. Their analysis covers both tabular representations and linear function approximation without explicit dimension-dependent terms in the convergence bounds. This creates a more unified guarantee than approaches that require substantially different treatments for the two representations.

The method also improves the condition-number dependence of sample complexity from quartic to quadratic, matching the type of efficiency available in the discounted setting. The contribution concerns policy evaluation under the analyzed sampling procedure. It does not directly establish a complete control algorithm or the same guarantees for arbitrary nonlinear value-function approximators.
icml-2026-bridging-the-gap-between-avera.tldr: A two-trajectory TD algorithm gives unified average-reward evaluation guarantees with improved condition-number dependence.

paragraphs: Public benchmarks can be contaminated by training data or exploited through repeated evaluation feedback. Keeping labels private does not fully prevent overfitting to a test set. CapBencher adds a detectable accuracy ceiling by retaining uncertainty about which valid answer is recorded as the benchmark target.

For each suitable problem, the method prepares several logically correct answers but randomly includes only one as the official solution. This lowers Bayes accuracy for a model without access to that random choice. Performance above the resulting ceiling becomes evidence of leakage or gaming, while the benchmark remains openly evaluable without fully revealing its ground truth.

Theoretical analysis and experiments across benchmarks, models, and training scenarios show effective detection of test-set overfitting. The contribution is an alarm embedded in benchmark design. Its interpretation depends on the randomized-answer construction and the corresponding accuracy bound, rather than treating any unusually strong result on an ordinary benchmark as proof of contamination.
icml-2026-capbencher-give-your-llm-bench.tldr: CapBencher randomizes among valid answers to create an accuracy ceiling whose violation signals benchmark leakage or gaming.

paragraphs: Language-model security agents can struggle when they reason without enough execution feedback or repeatedly discard lessons from previous attempts. Co-RedTeam organizes vulnerability analysis into coordinated stages intended to address those weaknesses. The framework combines security knowledge, code analysis, interaction, and reusable experience.

Separate discovery and exploitation stages allow agents to plan, execute, validate, and refine actions using observed execution results. Long-term memory stores prior trajectories so later work can benefit from earlier experience. The architecture is intended to mirror an iterative red-teaming workflow rather than a single static prediction about whether code is vulnerable.

Across security benchmarks and multiple backbone models, the system reports exploitation success above 60% and more than a ten-percentage-point improvement in detection. Ablations support the importance of execution feedback, structured interaction, and memory. These are benchmark capability results; the abstract does not establish the same success on arbitrary live systems or provide an unrestricted guarantee of security-analysis reliability.
icml-2026-co-redteam-orchestrated-securi.tldr: Co-RedTeam coordinates discovery, validation, and experience reuse to improve benchmark vulnerability detection and exploitation performance.

paragraphs: Neural operators must often process long sequences or large meshes, and latent-state designs can lose useful information when states are temporary or disconnected from coordinates. CoEvol-NO introduces a persistent state that evolves together with the mesh sequence. The relationship is bidirectional rather than a one-way encoding step.

Each layer follows a predictor-corrector pattern inspired by numerical methods. A predictor proposes a target, then an error-driven corrector refines the persistent state. The authors show that common direct-substitution and residual-update schemes can be understood as first-order approximations of this correction under different loss assumptions.

The analysis proves linear time complexity. Experiments on five standard benchmarks and two large industrial-design tasks report state-of-the-art performance. The contribution connects a persistent neural representation to a classical correction principle while preserving scalability. The abstract does not specify all complexity variables or benchmark error values, so those details require the full method and evaluation.
icml-2026-coevol-no-state-and-coordinate.tldr: CoEvol-NO jointly updates persistent states and mesh coordinates through error-driven predictor-corrector steps with linear-time complexity.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models promise parallel generation but often need many refinement steps for good text. Continuous-domain consistency training offers acceleration, yet its sample-space differential-equation formulation does not directly apply to discrete tokens. This paper develops a discrete counterpart based on exact posterior bridges between noise levels.

Multi-Path Discrete Consistency trains a denoiser to be path-invariant in expectation across those stochastic bridges. The resulting Consistent Diffusion Language Model uses a single-stage procedure without requiring a pretrained teacher. The framework also connects masked diffusion, continuous consistency models, and distillation through shared limiting or approximate formulations.

Experiments on conditional and unconditional text generation outperform strong discrete-diffusion baselines across sampling budgets, often including multi-stage distilled systems. The largest gains occur with few sampling steps. The contribution is both a principled discrete training objective and evidence of faster high-quality generation; the abstract does not provide a universal wall-clock speedup across hardware and model sizes.
icml-2026-consistent-diffusion-language-.tldr: Discrete posterior-bridge consistency trains diffusion language models for stronger few-step generation without a pretrained teacher.

paragraphs: Slate bandits choose a combination of items and observe one reward for the whole set. This paper studies contextual slates with generalized-linear rewards when the learner cannot update its policy freely every round. Such limits matter when adaptation itself is costly or operationally constrained.

The authors propose a batched algorithm using O(log log T) batches and a rarely-switching algorithm using O(Nd log T) parameter updates. Under a diversity assumption, they obtain regret bounds of O(Nd³ᐟ²√T) and O(Nd√T), respectively. Neither bound depends on the nonlinearity parameter that commonly appears in GLM-bandit analyses.

Both methods require only polynomial time in the number of item sets despite exponentially many possible slates. Simulations outperform limited-adaptivity baselines and remain competitive with a fully adaptive method, with an additional language-model example-selection application. The contribution combines limited updating, computational efficiency, and favorable regret under the stated item-diversity condition.
icml-2026-contextual-slate-glm-bandits-w.tldr: Efficient contextual slate-bandit algorithms retain strong regret guarantees with very few batches or policy updates.
